evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/rate_limit.rs:35 — `pub type InProcessRateLimiter<K> = Mutex<HashMap<K, RateLimitEntry>>;` is a process-local counter with no shared/Redis backing. The module's own doc comment (rate_limit.rs:18) already flags this: 'The counter is per-process; a Redis-backed counter (the sessions Redis is ...) [would be needed for distributed enforcement]'.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/mfa.rs:44 & :82 — the MFA recovery-code verify and MFA setup-verify endpoints (6-digit TOTP / recovery-code, mfa.rs:71 comment 'checks a 6-digit TOTP', verify at :307/:391 and :980/:985) are throttled ONLY by `static MFA_RECOVERY_RATE_LIMITER`/`MFA_SETUP_VERIFY_RATE_LIMITER: LazyLock<UserRateLimiter>` (in-process), 10 attempts/window. Across N horizontally-scaled api-server replicas behind the load balancer the effective online-guess budget is ~10*N per window, and every deploy/restart resets all counters — materially raising online TOTP/recovery-code brute-force feasibility against a 10^6 code space.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/documents/shares.rs:42 — `static SHARE_ACCESS_RATE_LIMITER: LazyLock<InProcessRateLimiter<String>>` throttles the public unauthenticated `POST /api/v1/documents/shared/{token}/access` password brute-force (added in response to prior finding code-review-api-handlers-share-pw-no-throttle). Same per-process limitation: the control it restored is bypassable by fanning attempts across replicas and is wiped on restart. auth/mod.rs (login/forgot-password) and voice_webhooks.rs share the identical in-process pattern.

Feasible fix already in reach: AppState carries a live `redis_client` (used for OAuth single-use state in routes/integrations/oauth_state.rs and for sessions), so these security-sensitive limiters can be moved to a shared Redis counter (atomic INCR + EXPIRE) to make brute-force throttling hold across replicas and survive restarts. This is a follow-on to the now-fixed 'no throttle' finding, not a duplicate: the throttle exists but is not distributed.
